malus, mala, malum

adjective; comparative pejor, superlative pessimus, declension

Bad in every sense: bad weather, bad bread, a bad book, a bad man. Short a: mālus is the apple tree (Quint. 1.7.2). The adverb is male, badly (see not bad). A bad illness or wound is gravis; a child who is being bad is improbus (see naughty); for food that has gone bad, see bad (of food).

Examples

  • dīcit vīlicus sēdulō sē fēcisse, servōs nōn valuisse, tempestātēs malās fuisse

    the bailiff says he did his best, the slaves were ill, the weather was badCato Agr. 2.2

  • ‘malum pānem’ inquis. expectā: bonus fīet

    ‘Bad bread,’ you say. Wait: it will turn good.Sen. Ep. 123.2

  • pējor, pējus

    worseTraupman 409

  • dēterior, dēterius

    worse (lower, inferior)Traupman 409

  • gravior, gravius

    worse (more severe)Traupman 409

See also not bad, naughty, bad, better, bad for you.
